Review Title: Do not trust these people!!! What a disappointment!!
Review Text: During my trip to Alaska, the most important thing to me was to take a tour on a float plane. I booked this the last day of our cruise, which was in Ketchikan Alaska. On our way into the port, I watched excitedly as one float plane after another left and flew in front of our balcony. I couldn't wait and told several friends and family members how excited I was to take this flight  that was scheduled for 4 PM. I got to the meeting place 15 minutes early when I received a phone call that the flight was canceled. When I inquired why it was canceled there was a pause and then the woman on the other end of the line told me there was a mechanical issue that they thought would be fixed in time for the flight, but they couldn't fix it. I found out shortly after from a person in the business that they called to try and help fill the plane that a mechanical wasn't the case at all. The plane wasn't full so they canceled it. On top of a HUGE disappointment. I was even more disappointed that they flat out lied to me. Had they been honest I might have even paid for the empty seats for this experience, but they never even gave me the chance. I called their number back and it went right to voicemail. I left 2 messages asking if perhaps they knew another pilot that could take me on a flight  but of course never heard back from them.  It's obvious  they care much more about how much money is in their pocket than they do about customer service or even honesty. I would never trust these people. They lost a lot more money by not even offering to let me pay for the empty seats and more importantly, lost respect, which is the one and only thing people in business have. What a total disappointment.

Review Text:
On 7/25/2023 we took the Misty Fjords flight seeing tour. There were a total of 8 passengers on a well maintained DHC-3.

The best I can say is that Taquan Air completely mailed it in. For the price it should have been significantly better. Buyer beware and spend your valuable money on other activities.

The total cost for all 8 was close to $3,000 for which we got a seaplane flight that fell well short of how it was hyped by the cruise line or on Taiwan Air’s site.

We expected that there would be narration by the pilot pointing out landmarks and notable features. The pilot didn’t utter a single word after boarding. Instead there was a cheesy pre-recorded narration that was spotty and difficult to understand. Passengers shouldn’t ask, “ are we at the Misty Fjords”.

The pilot, although clearly proficient, was going through the motions and was clearly disinterested in anything except for talking to his fellow pilots in the radio.

This was the only regrettable experience of the 2-week Alaskan experience. Don’t do it!!!

Review Text:
Schöner Ausflug zu einer Staatlichen-Lachsaufzuchtfarm, wo es auf Grund der extrem vielen Lachse im dortigen Fjord, entsprechend Bären, Seelöwen, Seeadler, Krähen, Möven usw. hat.
Der Hin- u. Rückflug mit dem Wasserflugzeug der Taquan Air Tours war ein geniales Erlebnis!
Im Fjord wurden wir von einer Rangerin in Empfang genommen und sofort über das Verhalten hier informiert. Vom ersten Moment an war klar, dass es hier Bären hat und zwar ohne Zaun dazwischen, eine neue Erfahrung!
Keine 20 Minuten durch den Wald marschiert und immer wieder mit Informationen über die Flora und Fauna gespiesen, gelangen wir zu einem Bach, an dem sich drei Bären mit Lachs vollstopften. Lange konnten wir diese beobachten u. fotografieren, Adler, Seelöwen, Krähen, Möven usw. liessen sich ebenfalls sehr fotogen ablichten.
Für Fotografen ein lohnender Ausflug ohne grosse Ansprüche zu haben.

Review Text:
Wir haben kurzentschlossen bei der Bronzestatue gebucht. Mit einem Transporter wurden wir zum Flughafen gefahren, wo wir bestens empfangen wurden. Nachdem wir die Formalitäten geklärt hatten, wurden wir nach Gewicht in das Flugzeug gesetzt. 10 Gäste und ein Pilot. Jeder Gast sitzt am Fenster und hat ein Headset zum mithören. Unser Pilot hat beste Musik abspielen lassen, was die grandiose Flugzeit und die Natur bestens untermalte. Hinflug über dem Wasser, Rückflug über einen Pass und die Wälder.
Am Zielort wurden wir von einer Frau empfangen, welche unsere Führerin auf der Tour war. Via einem gut ausgebauten Wanderweg dem Wasser entlang, liessen die Spuren der anwesenden Bären nicht lange auf sich warten. Gut informiert kamen wir bei den Aussichtsplattformen an. Bereits auf dem Weg zu diesen Plattformen, konnten wir in einiger Entfernung den ersten Bären beim Fischfang beobachten. Bei den Plattformen waren es diverse Bären, welche sich an der Vielzahl von Lachsen vollfrassen. Ebenfalls hatte es Weisskopfadler, Raben, Möven, Robben usw. zum beobachten.
Unsere Tour war in dieser Jahreszeit ein voller Erfolg!

Review Text:
We visited Ketchikan and did the seaplane excursion with Taquan Air Tours only about a month after a couple of highly publicized accidents involving the company in the summer of 2019. Even though the accidents occurred in close succession, it is important to understand how many of these excursions the company flies each day, each month, each year when no such accidents occur, and to consider how many automobile accidents happen daily on the interstate within just a few miles of ones home, or even at a nearby intersection, I think that the excursions do come with an element of danger, but not a ton more than driving to work each day. It seemed to me that our pilot knew his job very well, and that the plane was well-maintained, and that every precaution was taken to ensure a safe flight and landings. Having said that, this was, of course Ketchikan, Alaska, and the estuary/bay where we took off did have a small number of logs floating around that posed a potential danger during take off and landing, due to sometimes being visible only at the last moment. In fact, out of concern whether we may possibly have clipped one such log during take off, our pilot requested another pilot who took off shortly after us to fly by our right side to visually affirm that that the pontoon on that side had not taken any damage that might affect landing, which in fact it had not.
During the flight to Misty Fjords, the scenery was beautiful, and it was fun to land in one of the bays there and step out onto one of the pontoons for photos, which the pilot happily took for us.
In my opinion, all of the best adventures involve at least an element of danger, and the choice taken to avoid one perceived danger is all too often the choice that leads to a different totally unexpected accident, due to an overly-comfortable illusion of safety/security. This excursion was one of our trips highlights. We enjoyed it a lot, and believe most visitors would, too.

Review Text: My husband is a pilot and we love flying no matter the type or size of the airplane. This was our first floatplane flight ever and it totally exceeded our expectations. We were with four other passengers and were comfortable and secure. Our pilot was a retired air line pilot so anyone who worries about the experience of the pilot-relax, he had thousands of hours of flight time. We took off and flew right past our cruise ship and then headed for Misty Fjords National Monument. Our pilot had a perfect balance of commentary and quiet, accompanied by a great playlist for our time aloft. The scenery was beautiful-rugged mountains, pristine lakes, lush forests, and waterfalls. We flew past an eagle soaring-amazing! We landed on a lake in the middle of the mountains, stood out on the pontoons for a bit, reboarded and then took-off again. Our flight was about an hour and we would have been happy to stay up longer! We look forward to returning to Ketchikan and doing this again and maybe staying in a cabin for a week or so!! Thank you Taquan Air!

Review Title: Amazing Seaplane ride and breathtaking views of Misty Fjords
Review Text: My wife and I  booked our tour to Misty Fjords through Princess Cruise. I had mixed feeling about the tour because we could only get space on the first flight out of the day and I was not sure if we would be able to see much in Misty Fjords. There is a reason it is called MISTY Fjords. Ketchikan is surrounded by rain forest and it rains there all the time. We were told that if there are clouds our flight might not happen. When our cruise ship reached Ketchikan it was party cloudy. The forecast had slight chance of showers. Well by the time we boarded the small 6 seater seaplane sun had come out. It was our first time in a  seaplane. Taking off from  water was an interesting experience. Our pilot was experienced and knowledgeable about the area and shared interesting information through the whole flight. However, there were no microphones in our headset. so we could only hear our pilot but could not ask him questions. The headset were old also and at times there were lot of noise. The experience would have been much better if we had better (newer) headphones with microphones.  By the time we reached the fjords, the clouds and mist had cleared and the views were breathtaking. Our pilot flew the plane low enough through the fjords to really enjoy the spectacular scenery. We landed at a remote spot in the fjords and stepped out of the seaplane for about 5 to 10 mins. On the way back, our flight path was different than the one we took flying in to the Misty Fjords. We saw many bald eagles. Overall an enjoyable experience in a seaplane.

Review Title: Neets Bay Bears - Experience of a lifetime!
Review Text: What an amazing experience!  I will admit I was more than a little nervous about this excursion.  My husband and I were on an Alaskan cruise to celebrate our 20th anniversary.  We decided to splurge and purchased the excursion with Tiquan Air to take us to Neets Bay to view bears.  It was the hightlight of our trip for sure!!  Our pilot, Jake, took extra effort to make me feel comfortable and safe in the plane.  After a beautiful and smooth flight we landed at a remote location and was met by our guide Mark.  Mark was AWESOME!  He is the "perfect guide".  Mark obviouly has a gift for educating people about the Alaskan wilderness and bears, and no doubt he loves his job.  He took us to the most beautiful overlook so we could see bears feeding.  I noticed that Mark was constantly surveying the area and making sure we were safe.  At one point one of the bears came ONTO THE VIEWING PLATFORM with us!  I watched as Mark slowly positioned himself so that he stood between us and the bear all the while letting us know that he was going to keep us safe.   The bear trotted off up the trail that Mark led us on down to the platform. If one is traveling in this area of Alaska - this tour is a must!   It is amazing and worth every penny!

Review Title: Bear Watching in Margaret Creek ab Ketchikan
Review Text: Der Flug ab Ketchikan war interessant und gut, da ich mit einem Flugzeug noch nicht geflogen bin. Einmal als Bespaßung reicht es allerdings allemal. Der Zweck des Fluges war eindeutig, die Bären zu sehen. Nun, die Bären sind nicht gekommen! Und dadurch war auch der Sinn eines durch die Fliegerei sehr teuren Ausfluges absolut verfehlt. Beim Empfang durch den Naturalist war es ihm schon bewusst, dass er uns an der "Nase herumführt", als er so tat, dass uns bald etwas bäriges erwartet! Eine 3-köpfige Familie, die auch dabei war, war mehr als enttäuscht - da der Vater offensichtlich ein Fotograf war. Diese überteuerte Bear Watching sollte sich die Firma ersparen - es ist keine gute Werbung. Und die Piloten können leider nichts dafür, dass sie am Ende ohne Trinkgeld auskommen müssen! Ansonsten wäre sicherlich auch eine Angleichung an die Praxis bei Safaris möglich, wo sich die Fahrer gegenseitig per Funk informieren, wo welche Tiere sind und erst dann fahren sie in die Richtung los. Dieser Service müsste in dem Preis schon dabei sein!! Ich empfehle diese Art der Bear Watching nicht, und selber würde die Flugzeug-Variante auf keinen Fall wiederholen - da kann ich das Geld gleich aus dem Fenster werfen - und ohne Enttäuschung!

Review Text:
I had a confirmed booked through Alaska Shore Tours for the Neets Bay Floatplane bear watch tour. At the time I was not aware that Alaska Shore Tours had subcontracted the tour to Tarquan Air.
As the instructions indicated I was at the Ketchikan meeting point but no representative of the tour! After about twenty minutes waiting a member of my cruise ship came by and when I explained the issue took me inside the Visitor Centre. There was no one at the Tarquan Air booth and a neighbouring tourist operator phoned them for me to be told that the tour had been cancelled. I received no notification of this and had waited for over 25 minutes for someone from the company to arrive. He came to his booth after 30 minutes to explain that there were skieners on the Bay and the plane was unable to land.
That is not the fault of Tarquan Air but to have no representative at the designated meeting point on time nor to inform guests that the tour is cancelled is negligent.
On my complaint to both Alaska Shore Tours and Tarquan Air I was informed I should have phoned them to find out the situation! My complaint to the Ketchikan Tourist Authority met with a similar response and it appeared as though Tarquan Air and the local tourist authority are linked in some form.
Needless to say the highlight of my trip to Alaska, bear watching, was ruined. The failure to notify me of the cancellation meant that it was too late to organise another tour although I did manage to get a trip to Misty Fjord - not at all what I wanted.
Tarquan Air and Alaska Shore Tours gave an apology only after I emailed them both with my complaint and have given no compensation other than the refund of my bear watching tour cost.
I'm glad others had a good experience for their tours with this company. Mine was a waste of time and a huge frustration as well as very stressful.
To ensure that you are kept informed about a changing situation don't book with these companies but work through your cruise ship booking agency!!

Review Title: Misty Fjords Seaplane Excursion - Fantastic Experience
Review Text:
We booked very last minute through our cruise ship (Norwegian) because we hadn't really planned anything for Ketchikan and boy are we glad we did!
In reading the reviews I see a lot of complaints about waiting for the bus. I'll be honest and say that the tour had a "meetup" time of 10:30am, but the bus didn't show up until 10:45 or maybe even closer to 11, but I assumed that was deliberate to allow for stragglers/late-comers to make the pickup.
Once we got to the docks it was a pretty quick and efficient process. We were broken up into groups and assigned a pilot and then loaded onto the planes within 15-30 minutes. Our pilot had been flying for 40 years and provided both music and commentary as he flew us from ketchikan through the mountains to their floating dock. We had a solid 15 minutes to admire the view and snap photos and then we loaded up and flew back.
My husband and I have both spent time in small planes working on our private pilot licenses and the pilot was quick to notice and offer us the front seat (one on the way out, one on the way back). Even though the plane is only rated for VFR, the pilot had the "glass cockpit" terrain/attitude and a collision avoidance TCAS (or something similar) displays as well which made me feel really good about the company's commitment to safety especially when flying so close to the terrain and with so much competing air traffic (there were 2 other planes that took off at the same time and another 2 to 4 in the area on our flight out).
The Havilland Beaver is the perfect aircraft for these sorts of tours given its capacity and they use the modified versions which include additional trapezoidal windows behind the rear windows so that everyone has a view. Such an incredible experience, hauntingly beautiful and very professional/safe. I recommend it!

Review Text:
Fantastica esperienza! Si inizia con il trasferimento in pulman dalla nave alla sede di Taquan Air, e l'autista siccome eravamo in anticipo ci ha fatto fare un giro turistico della cittadina. Io che lavorando sulle navi da crociera ci sono stato centinaia di volte ho visto dei posti dove non sono mai stato.
Poi siamo arrivati alla Taquan Air, dove abbiamo conosciuto Adam, il nostro pilota di un De Havilland Otter. Grande personalita'. simpatico ed entusista del proprio mestiere.
Il volo e' stato grandioso, sia grazie al tempo che e' stato bellissimo che grazie ad Adam, che invece di mettere un nastro registrato ha commentato lui stesso il volo, con una musica soft rock di sottofondo.
Poi siamo arrivati a Neets' Bay, dove Neil (spero di ricordare il nome) ci ha fatto da guida, e ci ha portato per 15 minuti circa in una foresta dove c'erano molte testimonianze che gli orsi sono li', compresi alberi con i segni delle arrampicate o tane sotto le radici degli alberi.
Poi siamo arrivati dove i salmoni finiscono la loro corsa, ed ovviamente gli orsi vengono a cacciare i pesci. Subito c'era un orso, poi un altro, ma per un bel po' di tempo erano lontani. Quando mancavano 30 minuti al ritorno si sono avvicinati, ed au un certo punto erano a pochi metri da noi. Grandi opportunita' per foto e video!
Purtroppo poi siamo dovuti tornare, e Adam il nostro pilota ci ha fatto un regalo particolare, passando per un fiordo non famoso come Misty Fijord ma altrettanto bello. Un peccato che non sia piu' pubblicizzato, ma credo che i locals se lo vogliono tenere per loro, infatti Adam ci diceva che loro vanno sempre li' per camminate ed escursioni o hiking.
Un tour da non perdere con un tour operator fantastico!
Grazie mille!

Review Title: Neets Bay Bear Tours - great flight and we did see a couple of bears
Review Text:
We were sailing Carnival and next to last port of call was Ketchikan. We opted for the Neets Bay Bear Watch or tour...
When we arrived to the float plane port, Taquan airlines was our carrier.
Great pre-brief. If you have a camera back pack.. they might ask you to leave it there.. locked up. It will depend on type of airplane, amount and weight of passengers and ultimately the pilot. I had been briefed prior to and didn't take mine but mounted the large lens on the camera and had the smaller lens in my coat.
Pilot was great and described the flight and scenery the entire time we flew out and back.
It was a very hot day.. and low tide.. .the group before us told us they didn't see any bears.. Our guide told us it was iffy. We did see a few bear caves and marks where they climbed the trees. When we arrived at the fish hatchery... there were no bears and we waited and waited.. I did get a few good shots of eagles looking for a free lunch. Someone told our guide that there was a mother bear and cub on the way back down the trail. (short hike out and back by the way)... We found the bears and the guide made sure we stopped at 3 - 4 places to get good shots.
No one can control the: weather, tide, and bears... so be prepared for anything or nothing. Flight out and back was phenomenal. The pilot even offered to take pictures of us beside the airplane.. Great time.. thank you..

Review Title: A Highlight of our Alaskan Adventure
Review Text:
My family and I took a float plane over the Misty Fjords during our cruise through the Inside Passage of Alaska. My parents, husband, kids (6 & 9) and I all agree that this experience was one of the best memories of our trip.

The views are things that you only see on postcards. Evan, our pilot, was friendly and provided us a nice balance between telling us about the National Park and giving us time to take in the sights. My 9-year-old son was thrilled that he got to sit in the “co-pilot’s” seat and Evan was very kind in making him feel important.

We landed on a floating dock about half way through our flight and were able to get out and take in the beauty that surrounded us. Evan was nice enough to offer to take many pictures of our family that are now framed in our house.

If you are lucky enough to spend some time in Ketchikan, I would absolutely recommend a Taquan Air Tour.

Review Title: Anan Creek Bear Viewing Tour our of Ketchikan - Excellent Flight, Outstanding Guide
Review Text:
Last year, Taquan (pilot Dave and guide Mark Phillips) did an excellent job at getting us to Anan Creek. However, due to our ship's limited time in port last year, along with poor tidal conditions, we were not able to actually get to the trail head and take our tour. This year, we again booked our Anan Creek tour with Taquan and we were not disappointed. From the bus drive to their terminal, to their check-in and flight briefing process, to the flight itself, and to the tour guide - Taquan offers a safe, informative and exciting tour.

The checkin and safety briefing process was thorough, yet efficient (quick). We met with our pilot, Eric, immediately after the safety briefing, and he walked us down the pier to our plane. Eric got us situated on the plane, and then our tour guide arrived. To our pleasant surprise, our guide from last year - Mark Phillips - was again our guide this year! Within a few minutes we were skimming across the water and taking off from Ketchikan. Eric provided some commentary on various landmarks while we were en route to Anan Creek, and Eric's 45 minute flight from Ketchikan to Anan Creek was smooth and comfortable. At one point as we got near Anan Creek, we encountered a rain squall, and Mark and Eric communicated and made some adjustments which ultimately allowed us to safely land at the Anan Creek landing site.

For any tourists taking a float plane to Anan Creek, it is important to be aware that at low tide there can be significant logistics regarding where/how you get to the Anan Creek trailhead. When we arrived at Anan Creek, it was low tide - and Eric brought the plane to a small dock that was far enough off shore to avoid grounding the plane. Taquan had arranged a small boat to transport us from the dock to the shore, and that worked out very well.

If you remember any tip from this review, it is this: if you want to avoid the potential hassles and delays of low-tide arrivals at Anan Creek by float plane, make sure ahead of time that your pilot knows to putter into the entrance of the creek where the water is deep enough (even at low tide) for any float plane to drop off passengers just below the ranger briefing station. It is not worth your time, or the risk of grounding, to make land anywhere near the docks or the hut.

Let me say here that our guide, Mark Phillips, was awesome. Mark was friendly, knowledgeable, and he has the experience of having flown out to Anan Creek multiple times in the past. Mark was able to provide direct in-flight guidance to our pilot when weather conditions got a bit hairy. And Mark takes safety seriously: we were in bear country, and after we made land then Mark unpacked and holstered a weapon and bear spray - which made us feel safe on our hike.

After we got on land, and after Mark made the preparations for our hike to the bear viewing area, we met with the ranger at the base of the trail and listened to a briefing. We then set out on the approximately two-thirds of a mile hike up to the bear viewing area. As we got underway, Mark guided us in the proper way to group ourselves in case we encountered a bear on the trail. And Mark also provided expert commentary on plants and wildlife that we encountered on the hike. When we arrived at the bear viewing area, Mark helped us get signed up quickly so that we could get a slot in the bear viewing blind, and Mark continued to provide awesome commentary about different bears and occurrences that we saw when we were up at the viewing platform. I can't say enough great things about Mark; we highly recommend him if you can get him for your tour.

Taquan runs a great airline, they employ an enthusiastic and knowledgeable staff (including expert guides), and our safety was their priority from start to finish. Taquan ultimately provided us with a fantastic and memorable tour, and we highly recommend them for anyone looking to take a flight/float plane tour out of Ketchikan.

Review Text:
Trip Advisor review

Our family group of 5 decided to take the Floatplane bear watching shore excursion. It was a bit pricey but we expected it because you’re flying in a floatplane Believe me when I say we all agreed it was definitely worth the money.

They picked us up where the cruise ships dock and took us where the floatplanes were. We were given our instructions and loaded on the plane. Our pilot was JR and he was wonderful and knowledgeable. The takeoffs and landings and even the flight itself were all smooth, actually smoother than we thought they’d be. We flew for 30-40 minutes and landed. We were met by our guide and we walked an easy trail for 10-15 minutes and arrived at a platform high up and next to a stream. Besides the mother bear and her cub that we walked by on the trail, there were at least 15 bears catching salmon. Oh and a bald eagle too. The time we spent there was unbelievable watching the bears in the water fishing salmon out of the stream and some even fighting over their catches. Could have stayed there for hours as it was so fascinating. They allowed us 1-1 1/2 hrs before we headed back. Once again our pilot JR treated us well with a nice flight back. We were then taken back to the cruise ship.

We all agreed if we ever come back to Ketchikan we are definitely doing this again. No doubt!

Review Title: Incredible Flight. Forrest is da PILOT
Review Text:
First of all the scenery is an 11 out of 10. Just stunning. You fly through mountain passes with granite faces, waterfalls, thick forests, lakes and land in a pristine fjord. It’s like a dream. I’ll remember it forever.

Forrest Carpenter was our pilot. He is a young man and a third gen commercial pilot. I have no doubt that some day he will be in the left seat of a big Boeing, but for now you get his superb flying talents in an ancient (but safe) DH Beaver float plane with a Pratt and Whitney R-985 radial piston engine. It is THE ultimate classic bush plane. It is to bush flying what the DC 3 was to commercial air travel.

He LOVES flying this historic plane (usually N67667) and takes really good care of it. He is very attentive to mixture, throttle, manifold pressure and cylinder head temp which should please the plane’s owners.

The landing he made in Misty Fjord was literally PERFECT. I have never seen better. Zero perceptible vertical deceleration. He just NAILED it. I’ve experienced really good float plane landings but this was a cut above. It just can’t get any better.

Forrest knows the local area well and gives a personally narrated tour, not a canned sound track. He provides info on geology, geography, aviation and local history as he flies you through the most beautiful scenery on planet Earth.

Take the Misty Fjord flight tour. Worth every penny. If you are lucky you’ll get Forrest as your pilot.

Review Text:
Great group of people but may be suffering from their own success. The operation appears top notch like others I have reviewed. But they seem to lack the ability to easily manage the large groups they arrive with the cruise ships. They do have plenty of room, both inside and out, it seemed they simply needed a few more teammates to herd the tourists.
Every person I met was professional and courteous, but often seemed busier than they may have been prepared to be. Our pilot, Ed, (I kept calling him Mike for some reason) was competent, and an Alaskan by birth so he was keenly knowlegible on the local info. However his music playlist interfered with some of his narration.
The aircraft are like those many other operators use in AK, the venerable dehavilland Beaver and Turbo Otters. Well maintained and comfortable. We arrived on the hottest day this summer so we were a bit toasty on our flight. The beaver offers good visibility and the headsets kept the wind and radial engine noise to a dull rumble. The flight lasted a little more than an hour and our pilot made a wide pattern over Annette Island, allowing my wife, who 20 years earlier landed with the Marines to assist in road building to see the fruits of those labors.
Well worth the time and money, you won’t be disappointed.

Review Text:
Like a previous reviewer, I booked this trip as part of my Alaska Inside Passage cruise and wasn't sure if I would really enjoy it. However the Tajuan Air and the team running this tour really did provide a fabulous experience and I'm pleased not to have missed it. You are allocated a float plane & pilot according to the weight / size distribution each float plane can carry, I shared the plane with 5 other people.

To participate in this tour you need to be able to independently get yourself onto the fabric float plane steps and up into your seat safely. Everyone receives a safety briefing and because there's no room for backpacks or bags on the plane, you're allocated a box with the float plane number to safely leave your belongings.

Before even setting off, I was a whale & large jelly fish in the harbour so I was hopeful of enjoying the flight. Our pilot was Mike, young & really laid back but experienced and knowledgeable all the same. We flew across lakes and mountains and into the Misty Fjords monument on a gloriously sunny Alaskan day and the scenery was amazing, no wildlife but that's not the point of this tour. Mike landed our float plane in the most peaceful and beautiful location within the fjords for a 10-15 minute stop, it was really breathtaking and a real privilige.
I'm glad to have taken this tour despite my reservations and suggest you gove ot a go too!

Review Text:
Last week we did the seaplane tour of the Misty Fjords on Taquan Air Tours. The views were spectacular. However, breathing in diesel fumes while in-flight was not fun. Anyway, after landing in the water in the fjords, we were allowed to get out of the plane onto one of its floats without life vests. According to the pilot, the dark waters were about 300 feet deep. Once we got out, the pilot asked us to scoot on over as much as possible to the front of the plane's float. However, once you go past the pilot's cabin, there is nothing to hold onto and the float gets narrower. Following the pilot's request, my teenage daughter, who was second in line from the front, decided to pass the girl in front of her who was holding on to the last piece of equipment on the front part of the fuselage. So now my daughter, who is not a very good swimmer, ended up balancing herself without holding onto anything near the front of the float. I asked her to get back so she could hold onto something as what she was doing was dangerous. She said no because she was following the pilots instructions and practically could not get back because the float by now was packed with most of the 10 passengers and the pilot. After about 5 minutes of standing on the front edge of the float where it is much narrower, I noticed her losing and then regaining her balance for a bit. If she had fallen in the water, with her parka and heavy clothing, she would have definitely gone under. I immediately yelled at her to get back in the plane which she did. When we got back on land, apparently someone had already told the Taquan staff of this incident. And when I brought it up with them, the answer I got was that the pilot will be given a talk about this.

What surprises me is how can something like this get past the safety inspectors? As a minimum, during all the pre-flight safety briefings, Taquan Air should address the safety of passengers while they are out of the plane on the float over deep dark waters and provide its passengers with life vests. They also need to make sure passengers are not exposed to high levels of diesel fumes while in flight.

Review Title: Neets Bay Bear Watch & Flightseeing - Incredible experience!
Review Text:
The Neets Bay Bear Watch & Flightseeing tour was one of the highlights of our cruise on the Star Princess. The entire experience was well-organized and well-executed.

My wife and I started the tour by meeting a representative from Alaska Shore Tours (Taqan Air Tours) on the pier just a few steps from our cruise ship. She was holding a sign with the excursion code clearly visible so we knew without a doubt that we were in the right place.

We were directed to a waiting bus, which was a very short walk from where we met the first representative. Once everyone attending the tour was loaded, we were driven to the marina where the planes were docked.

They presented a safety video and then directed us down a ramp onto the dock where the plane was waiting. Our pilot helped us onto the plane, checked to make sure everyone was properly buckled in and showed us how to use the headsets. He started the plane, taxied into open water, and then we took off.

This was our first time flying in a float plane. Takeoff and landing were quite smooth compared to typical wheeled planes. Seeing such a beautiful area from a relatively low altitude (compared to commercial jets) was amazing! The area around Ketchikan is so beautiful.

After a 20 minute flight, we arrived at Neets Bay. Our guide met us on the dock and gave us a short safety talk about how to behave around bears - what to do and what not to do. Then he led us up a ramp to a woodsy area. We were immediately able to see a marshy area with at least 2 dozen eagles.

The guide took us down a short trail and pointed out many signs of bear activity - scat (feces), claw markings on trees, and several plants that the bears had eaten. At the end of the trail (about 1/4 mile) was an open area with the fish hatchery.

Just as our group arrived at the fish hatchery, we heard muted "oos" and "ahhs" from another two groups that had arrived before us - bears! There were 2 bears within 50 yards, one was climbing into a spillway next to a waterfall and the other was a bit further downstream. We quickly grabbed our cameras and started making photos and videos. Just a few minutes later, we saw another adult bear and two cubs a bit further down. The bears picked several salmon out of the spillway and stream. (I'm sure people who see this every day may laugh at my amazement, but for someone who has never seen a bear outside of a zoo this was quite breathtaking!)

After quite a while of watching the bears and some nearby eagles, we (sadly) made our way back down the trail to the dock for our flight back the marina and bus ride back to the pier.

Review Text: Taquan is situated across the channel from the Ketchikan Airport, a 5 minute ride on the ferry. With wheeled luggage an easy hop from the terminal. No taxi required. I showed up and had a couple hours to wait for my float plane to Pt. Baker, and needed to purchase a box of groceries to ship out with me. The guys nearby the desk overheard me asking which store packed in boxes to ship, and they volunteered to drive me to the store, maybe a mile or so down the road. They made it sound that they were going that way already. To my surprise, they not only were not, but waited for me in the parking lot and returned me to Taquan. Partially cloudy day, beautiful flight delivering me right to the float in "Baker". Two weeks later... pick up on time, again unusually clear weather and back in Ketchikan. I asked for a cab, the gal asked my destination and called the Inn at Creek Street for a shuttle. Taquan held my 50 pounds of King salmon and bear in their freezer overnight. When I returned they grabbed my luggage, the box of fish and took me in their skiff to the float plane dock across the channel to check in for my return flight. The lad even offered to schlep my box up the long steep incline! Not ready to admit 65 too old to heft a 50 pound box to my shoulder and pull a suitcase and rod up the ramp... I declined... I am astonished at how seamlessly and with such a generous spirit ALL the employees anticipated every move to make my transport a breeze. No worries, sit back and watch the amazing scenery that is SE!

Taquan provides headphones so you can hear the pilot as he provides commentary on the flight. (It also helps with the engine noise.) There really isn't anywhere to go other than climb down onto the pontoon. Or sit in the plane. But the act of landing and taking off in the distant lake is probably the quintessence of Alaska.

Review Text:
The natural environment of Southeast Alaska is accessible in limited ways: by foot, by boat and by air. What the last loses in the way of intimacy is more than made up for in breadth. Add a water landing in Punchbowl Lake and you even recover some of that intimacy.

We booked this tour on the dock, saving $50 over the price on the ship ($209 v. $259) Our group of four joined five others on an 11 passenger DHC Otter. Everyone gets a window seat (and one lucky person gets the right hand seat in the cockpit). Our pilot, Chuck, demonstrated excellent airmanship, local knowledge and humour (as well as strong DJ skills!)

If you aren't a regular float plane passenger, be aware that the plane is small and winds in the narrow inlets and fjords can be changeable. Bumps are to be expected. If you are a regular float plane passenger, be aware that these Otters carry only 11, whereas Harbour Air packs in 17 between Vancouver and Victoria. You'll have plenty of space.

I forgot our pilot's name, which is unfortunate because he was very knowledgable on the area and funny as well. The planes are pretty old, but well maintained and, according to our pilot, very reliable.

You set out over the cruise ships and Ketchikan towards the fjords. It takes about 20-30 minutes to get into the national park and the views are spectacular. We ended up landing on the water in the middle of the fjords and were able to get out onto the side of the plane to look around and take pictures. We expected more wildlife on the tour, but only saw a bunch of seals lying on a beach from a long distance. We asked our tour guide and he said that there are very rarely wildlife spottings on this tour. The tour is amazing nonetheless, but that's just an expectation to having going into the tour.

We had an amazing time and would highly recommend.

Review Title: The highlight of three weeks in Canada and Alaska!
Review Text:
Having travelled from Calgary to Vancouver on the Rocky Mountaineer, then spent a week,on Vancouver Island, followed by a cruise to the Hubbard glacier and nearly back we little thought that the undoubted highlight of the trip was to be found in Ketchican.
I mean the place has 160 inches of rain a year for starters and having had the float plane rides at Juneau cancelled due to low cloud we expected the same at Ketchican.
Luckily we were wrong and put ourselves down for the Taquan Air Tours trip to the Misty Valleys. Initially down to fly on a larger float plane with a taped commentary we were part of a group of four at this the fag end of the season.
Our plane then was a De Havilland Beaver manufactured in 1956 according to Tony or Orville our pilot for the day. Tony was great, a local chap with a wealth of local knowledge. The best way to describe him would be to try and imagine a mix of Henry Fonda and Hawkeye Pearce.
After warnMing up the engine we were off. To say the scenery was fab would do him an injustice, it was soul searching. Scale and magnificence were there in buckets. He told us the fire service let out cabins in the woods in the area for the ultimate get away from it experience. He even landed on a mountain lake and we got some great pictures.
The time came and went all too soon, but the memory will last a lifetime.
So many thanks to the self proclaimed antique plane and antique pilot ( not)!

My kids (ages 22-28) wanted to see bears on our trip and we saw at least 10 of them. It was early in the season, so bears were not guaranteed. Then you get out with a guide and do a short hike (15-20 min) to the ranger station at Anan Creek--need to be able to walk a mile over rocky terrain. Review Title: First below, now above...an amazing place from any angle!
Review Text: We've done boat excursions through Misty Fjords before and it is an incredible experience. However, this time....unplanned, as we headed back to the ship we meandered through the excursion extravaganza and were interested in trying it by air this time. Scheduled a tour that allowed us time to head back to our stateroom and drop off our goodies and head back to the excursion desk. Much to our disappointment, we were the only two to sign up so they had to cancel however Taquan Air Tours was right next door and had a tour open for only one hour later. We were a little concerned about getting back for our 4:30 departure. Taquan explained if they didn't get us back in time, they would just have to fly us to our next port of call and they weren't really interested in getting into that. So with our fears extinguished, I took a deep breath and said Yes! (I never was a big fan of my feet being more that 25ft. above ground) And I have to say any fear of flying vanishes quickly once you get used to the tiny bouncing air currents (smoother than riding in car)...it was magical. Our very experienced pilot gave us to option of either listening to his live narration with his own mix tape...or the 'canned', pre-recorded voice over describing the area in general. Everyone on board voted for our pilot, (I believe it was Tim's) voice. His knowledge of the area and expertise in navigation assured us of the right choice. We landed on a lake high above sea level and was able to get out and breath in the pristine air, take photos and absorb the scenery. Upon take off, we lifted off right on top of the 1,000 foot waterfall....very impressive and dramatic! This really is a very different perspective of an incredible beautiful place on Earth....try not to miss it!

Review Title: WOW - WOW - WOW -  This was my #1 excursion during my 7-day Alaskan cruise
Review Text:

One passenger rides, "shotgun" in the co-pilot seat. We had a large group go, and they even took a 1-year old up.

You meet at their, very comfortable, building, watch a safety video, then are escorted to the dock by your pilot to your plane. Our pilot, Brentwood, was very experienced, safe, knowledgeable, and really engaging. I felt incredibly safe. I think the planes are powered by 9-cylinder engines. LOTS of torque. I couldn't believe how effortlessly the plane got airborne.

You fly about 30 minutes out, land in a remote lake, walk out onto the pontoons for about 15 minutes, then take off and fly back to the dock.

We flew at 3K feet. The views were beyond words. "Stunning, beautiful, breath-taking, spectacular", I could go on and on. I will never forget this excursion.

Some of the views may make the queasy a little shaky, but the experience will be worth it. Even though you're flying at 3K feet, some of the mountains you'll fly over will look like you're clearing them by only a couple hundred feet. Flying into the valley to land on the lake made my wife a little uneasy, but she was happy to do it.

Our 5-year old son fell asleep ten minutes into the trip. He never woke up for the landing/take-off on the lake, or the landing back by the dock.

Review Title: Taquan Air Great Tour but don't appreciate the dishonesty
Review Text:
When we arrived in Ketchikan on Tuesday, June 23, 2015, it was a beautiful day so we decided to book a seaplane excursion of the Misty Fjords. We ended up at Taquan Air and everyone was friendly and they showed us a safety video and told us that Taquan Air had a 100% safety rating. This eased my nerves. Due to the company overbooking, our group of 7 people had to go on the Cessna Caravan, a very nice plane, a little bigger than the DeHavilland Beaver (my husband was disappointed we didn't fly the Beaver but loved the Caravan), and our pilot, Kevin, was wonderful and gave us an amazing tour of the Misty Fjords and landed on a beautiful lake where we were able to get out on the pontoons. This excursion was a highlight of our trip to Alaska until two days later when we heard about the tragic crash of a seaplane doing the exact same excursion where all 9 people on board perished. I reassured myself that Taquan Air had a better safety record than ProMech Air, until I came across the below article.

The article made me feel betrayed by Taquan Air, and stupid for not doing more of my own research. The Cruise Lines and the tour companies seem to be too driven by profits that they may not cancel flights when necessary due to bad weather and are enticed into telling customers lies about their safety records so people won't back out of excursions. I still would've taken the flight had Taquan told me about the 2007 incident, but now I'll never fly with them again.

I'm giving a rating of 3 (wish it could be 2 1/2) because the Pilot, Kevin, was amazing and he seemed like an excellent pilot and made everyone feel very comfortable and deserves 5 stars, but the companies dishonestly about the crash in 2007 deserves ZERO stars.

Alaska News
As Southeast Alaska plane crash victims' life stories emerge, so do echoes of 2007 accident
Nathaniel Herz
June 27, 2015
He cited the 2007 crash that also happened during a tour of Misty Fjords, which an NTSB report a year later blamed on pilot error and inadequate supervision of the Southeast Alaska tour industry by the Federal Aviation Administration. Subsequent recommendations by the NTSB included the installation of webcams in the area and special weather training for tour pilots.

2007 Misty Fjords crash

Weather in Ketchikan the day of the crash was unsettled, with scattered showers and wind gusts hitting 26 mph.

“Equally impressive are the flight challenges posed by such dramatic terrain and volatile weather conditions,” the filing said.

In the 2007 crash, Ketchikan’s Taquan Air Service had sent three planes on Misty Fjords flight tours.

All three planes were flying through a shallow mountain pass known as “the cut.” The first plane made it through and the third plane’s pilot turned around and took a different route after running into what he described as a “wall of weather” — rain, fog and low clouds — according to news reports.

The second plane, a de Havilland Beaver, crashed in a box canyon and slid 250 feet down an embankment. All five people aboard were killed.

The pilot, 56-year-old Joseph Campbell, had 25 years of commercial aviation experience, but only seven hours of flying experience in Alaska when he was hired by Taquan to fly that summer.

Review Text:
As first-time-and-maybe-only-time Alaska visitors (via cruise ship), we signed up for an excursion romantically called “Misty Fjords by Floatplane” at Ketchikan. Wow, we are SO glad that fancy title materialized as Taquan Air on a day that was beautifully clear (duh, “misty” sounds really great, but you wouldn’t be able to see much if it were really misty…).

Anyway, we were loaded onto busses at the dock, had a short and well-narrated drive through Ketchikan, and delivered to the floatplane terminal. After the safety video we were divided into groups of (about) six, introduced to our pilot (Chad), and walked down to the waiting plane. What happens next will probably vary, depending on your plane and pilot, but in our case the seating was: first row = pilot and one guest, second row = two guests; third row = two guests, back row = 1 guest. Chad asked who wanted to ride shotgun with him, and two guests, who happened to both be pilots themselves, asked for that seat. No problem: we made a planned stop halfway through the flight, and the two pilot-guests got to trade places. Actually any of us could have changed places, but there was no need; every seat is a window seat!

Our plane was equipped with two-way headphones, so we got to hear Chad’s enthusiastic and knowledgeable description of the pretty awesome scenery - and the bonus technical questions-and-answers between Chad and the two pilot-guests. Not every flight would be that lucky. We had helicoptered in Skagway, taken the gondola in Juneau, but this scenery was the most spectacular of any that we had seen.

About halfway through the flight Chad spotted a nice landing spot on a lake with no other people, so we made a water landing and had the option of stepping out on the pontoons and/or trading places. It’s perfectly safe, but the idea of being surrounded by mountains and having nothing beneath you but a pontoon and sixty feet of water does give you a proper perspective on and appreciation of your wilderness environment. I wish that we could have spent the day hopping through five or six more lakes - each one more beautiful than the last. MAJOR TIP: be sure to set your camera to movie mode for some shots; still shots are good, but movies, especially on smartphones that you’ll always have with you when you get back home, are the only way to capture the changes in the landscape - and of course your take-offs and landings.

Happy landing back at the dock, back to the busses, and back to the cruise ship.

The thrill of hearing the thump thump of the big radial engine and then lifting off effortlessly into the sky from the water was a thrill in itself. However when we flew over some sheep and then some bears and landed on a very small lake deep into the national forest where there were no people and no roads the majesty of it all started to sink in. Our pilot Adam, explained in detail all that we were seeing and actually landed a second time to show us a particular site that most don't see. The steep cliffs, narrow passes, pristine lakes and of course the clouds that make up the "mist" of the Misty Fjords was just plain awesome. Though the trip is not inexpensive, worth every penny and then some. The personality and non scripted narration from Adam and his extremely proficient skill had everyone very relaxed and thrilled all at the same time.

Again, a trip of a lifetime and not to be missed. Would do it all over again in a heartbeat!

Review Title: They Went the Extra Mile - Thank You!
Review Text:
My wife, myself plus another couple tried to book a trip to Anan a few months in advance of our trip this past July. Every float plane company we called said that we were too late to book as there are only 60 visitor permits for this park issued for each day. All except one company and one person. A special SHOUT OUT to Danita Scott for convincing me to trust her and her going the extra mile to make this trip happen!! She was the only one to contact me back and inform me that 48 or 72 hours prior to the day we wanted to go 12 more permits are released and she would do all she could to obtain four permits for us. Our group committed money down to hold a float plane that would be refundable if the permits were not obtained. Danita and our tour guide AJ came through for us and got the permits! Now for the rest of the story.

A van picked us outside the cruise ship and took us to the Taquan Air offices. There we met our lovely and talented pilot Amanda (I think my name memory if right) and A.J. our guide. Our pilot could me a model but chose to be a pilot. Our group was glad she was our pilot. She took us and our guide on about a 45 minute float plane ride to Anan to see bears eat salmon from the stream.

Once arriving to the site our guide A.J. took control. A.J. had a pistol on his hip and a shotgun on his side. Our group was guided on about a 3/4 mile hike to an area controlled by the park to observe the bears. There are platforms at this site over the stream and also a blind that observers get 15 minutes at a time to watch the bears up close and personal. While we were there for a couple hours we observed over 20 different black bears coming to the stream to fish. Eagles flying all over too. It was AMAZING! It was like we were in the zoo cage (platform with only rails) and the bears were out in the open. The stream was "black" with so many salmon. A.J. did a great job explaining all the nature in the area and some of his past experiences. Our pilot was waiting for us after we hiked back to the start of the trail.

There are pictures attached. This tour is not always available since the fish do not always run the stream. Taquan Air Tours offer other options that can be purchased. This was one of the two top tours our group took while in Alaska for twelve days. We are so thankful Danita Scott talked me into trusting her and Taquan Air. You just start to wonder when you are asked to pay half in advance to someone you have never met!

THANK YOU to everyone involved from our Iowa group!

Review Text:
We booked this trip through our Disney cruise. The day we went the weather was beautiful. But Ketchikan is in an artic rain forest so I understand these tours are often cancelled. Our pilot was telling us the day before it was pouring rain, and all flights had been cancelled. Wind and fog are also issues, so booking a Misty Fjords flight is a bit of a gamble.

The planes are small (we had 5 passengers in our plane, all with a window view). They are also old (our pilot explained the Dehavilland Beavers aren't manufactured anymore), but apparently folks in Alaska rely upon these planes to get around. The pilot was very friendly, and had logged a lot of hours. They were careful to balance our weight out. The view from the jump seat, where my brother sat, is the best. The Fjords are beautiful. We saw snow covered mountains, and beautiful forests. We saw eagles and bears down below. The ride at times could be bumpy but the pilot was careful to adjust, and we even got a fly by over our cruise ship. My 5 year old travelled with us...I thought for sure he'd freak out and not go through with it but he did, and pilot was very friendly and even showed my enthusiastic son all about the controls. So all in all, a wonderful trip.

There were a few things that suprised me in our litigious society-- the safety briefing was a little short and you don't have to sign a bunch of waivers....the docks had no safety railings and a bit of a steep incline which could get slippery...we stopped at a fjord and could get out on the pontoons to look around. It was refreshing, however, that lawyering up hasn't come to Alaska yet, so enjoy it while you can.

Great service, wonderful views, and an excited 5 year old. A wonderful trip. I recommend, though there is a moderate possibility your trip may get cancelled due to weather concerns, and knowing such flights are not entirely risk free.

Review Title: A Misty Day at the Fjords
Review Text:
We recently took a flight seeing trip to Misty Fjords with Taquan Air. We chose this company because of the B1G1 free coupon offered in the Toursaver coupon book. I really didn't know what to expect but the company was very professional and well run. We were picked up at the ship and driven to the office. It was a really nice and professional looking office. It looked like a pretty big scale operation (I think I was expecting a mom and pop type of office). We watched a video and soon were on our way. They had several planes running that day and we were with another couple on our plane (so just 4 of us). We took off and headed past the town of Ketchikan (and our ship) to Misty Fjords. It lived up to it's name. It was misty but it was also beautiful. There was turquoise water, steep granite cliffs, waterfalls and even a rainbow. We landed on the water in the middle of one of the fjords and got out on the float for a few minutes. The pilot did a wonderful job on the take offs and landings.
The negatives for me were several. Most were not a big deal but I want you to know what to expect.
I was in the back of the plane and it was FREEZING, and I don't say that lightly. The seals around the door were non-existant and it made for a very uncomfortable ride. On the way back I rode in the front and it was warm up there.
My stomach was also revolting the entire way.....especially on the way back. I would definitely take some dramamine. It is better to be safe than sorry. I was eyeing that sea sickness bag and praying I wouldn't have to reach for it. I kept staring at the horizon and breathing really deep. Kind of took a little away from the trip for me.
Lastly, (but also initially)...when we excited our cruise ship and went to meet them where the map indicated, we also called them and let them know we were there. We waited and waited. Finally, someone from the port came up and asked if we needed help. We told him who we were waiting on and he indicated that they were in a different spot today. We went over there and the driver told us it was a good thing we showed up because he was about to leave us. When I shared with him that we were waiting in the correct spot and that we had even contacted the main office and let them know where we were he said that he didn't answer his cell phone so he couldn't have known this. This irritated me and I would have been extremely upset if we had been left behind...but we weren't so bigones and all that. Just be aware. (0therwise the company was really professional and I blame the driver, not the company)
I thought the fjords were very pretty. They didn't blow me away like some of the reports I read. I don't know if it is because we are from Colorado or if it is because we have seen some amazing places like this before (or because I was green to the gills :)) but it wasn't my favorite thing in Alaska we did. Once again, not a reflection on the company (that I am reviewing) at all. Except for the "mix up" (see how kind I can be) at the beginning, they were great.
Hope this helps!

Review Text:
Let me first state that my wife doesn't like to fly in small planes, and she was very nervous about the water part. But being the trooper she is she agreed to go for me. We did book this through our cruise ship and upon leaving the ship immediately boarded their bus. We had a great informative ride to the airport and learned a lot about Ketchikan. After a short briefing about safety and so forth we were introduced to our pilot Adam.

Adam led us out to our plane, the only float plane you should see Misty Fjords in a DeHavlland Beaver. If you fly in anything else you are shortchanging yourself. We strapped in and away we went.

The scenery. The amazing awe inspiring scenery. Words cannot describe what you will see. Glass lakes, waterfalls everywhere, sheer cliffs and more beauty that the mind can process. Adam took us close up to the rock faces and through mountain peaks for an unclose view. We then landed on a lake of smooth glass and left the aircraft to stand on a pontoon and enjoy the most quiet majestic view I have ever seen. We saw a brown bear at a stream which fed into the lake and many bald eagles. Departing the lake I was able to sit in the right seat next to Adam which made the flight back even better.

I didn't want this flight to end but couldn't talk Adam into it. Once out of the aircraft my wife gave Adam a big hug and thanked him for a wonderful flight. I'm not sure if she loved the flight or just thought he was cute. I am thinking about taking a trip back to Ketchikan with some friends to fish and I will definitely be flying with Taquan Air Again. By the way I take my safety seriously and so does Taquan Air. I check out all of the float plane tours before I left for Alaska and in my opinion Taquan Air is hands down the best.

Review Title: Great float plane experience and bear watching
Review Text: We pre- booked this bear watching experience with Taquan Air for our Ketchikan port visit. We were picked up by the Taquan shuttle at the port then given a video briefing at the Taquan office. We were then greeted by our pilot and boarded the 6 passenger float plane. The weather was sunny and water was like glass so we had perfect conditions for viewing the spectacular scenery as we flew to Prince of Wales Island for our bear watching at Traitor's Cove. Our pilot provided commentary  through our headphones, describing the scenery and history. He is a seasoned local pilot so was very knowledgeable and informative. Upon arrival at Traitor's Cove, we were greeted by the bear viewing guide who transported us by van on the short ride to the creek. There was already a black bear busy fishing in the creek and throughout our stay at the creek there were 1-2 bears busy catching the plentiful salmon. On the flight back to Ketchikan our pilot spotted 2 Humpback Whales and circled overhead for us to get a great aerial view of these giants. This was my first float plane experience and it was fantastic....flight, scenery and bears!

Review Text:
I took a HAL cruise in June 2010 and booked this excursion through the ship. The bus was there to pick us up right on time but there was a bit of a traffic jam of buses, so we got to Taquan Air a few minutes late. There they put us through a quick safety briefing and got us out to the floatplanes. The experience of getting into a plane that was sitting in the water and then taking off and landing on water was really difference and interesting. I'm glad I got to try it at least once.

My plane had the pilot and three passengers. I thought that was good, it looked like the plane could hold more. We all got a window seat, however the same person sat in the front both there and back; I think that could have been rotated since we got out at Misty Fjords.

The beginning of the flight was kind of average but once we got into Misty Fjords it was just break taking! This does not happen to me, but I literally teared up a bit as we flew through the area, past the solid walls of granite plunging to the water. It was just so beautiful and pure, it was really amazing. It's just about impossible to describe. I don't want to oversell it, but for me, I've done a lot of traveling, and few natural wonders have hit me as hard as this one.

The pilot few around a bit and pointed out a brown bear on the ground. That happened so fast I didn't get a picture. We landed in one of the lakes and got out and stood on the pontoons of the plane. The pilot came around and took a picture of each of us standing outside of the plane. We had a shorter stop since our bus had been late. Then we got back in and flew back to Taquan Air. My only issue was that I missed some stuff that was on the same side of the plane both times, with me on the wrong side. I thought possibly we could have switched or the pilot could have gone wide so both sides could see.

Overall, I don't know how much of a difference it makes what company you fly with. Taquan Air was fine and I have nothing to compare them to, my five star rating has more to do with the beauty of the Misty Fjords. They did have a gift shop and I got a nice purple fleece with the Taquan Air logo. At the end, we got back on the bus and were dropped back by the cruise dock.
